supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS proxy requests from WS-TWEBER-01 were to update.medledger.com. Successful requests are recorded at 13:37:04, 13:47:10, 13:51:53, 13:56:20, 14:02:07, and 14:06:22 UTC; a request at 13:41:37 was denied.

Endpoint network events attribute these update.medledger.com connections to PID 3784, C:\Program Files\MediLedger\medledgerupd.exe, which was launched on WS-TWEBER-01 shortly before the connections began.

The observed destination and roughly five-minute recurrence are consistent with the inventory-listed MediLedger updater behavior, which checks update.medledger.com about every five minutes; the evidence therefore supports a benign explanation for the alerted activity.

The observed requests used the explicit proxy at 10.51.20.30:8080 and were logged as CONNECT tunnels to the update host, rather than as direct connections from the workstation to the public HTTPS destination.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records identify CONNECT destinations and tunnel metadata, but the successful HTTPS tunnel contents are not shown, so the specific requests, responses, or any downloaded update cannot be verified from these records.
The proxy records show a Chrome user-agent string even for requests attributed by endpoint telemetry to medledgerupd.exe; these records do not establish why that user-agent was used.
The available process records do not include a file hash or signature validation for medledgerupd.exe.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the content of the successful HTTPS exchanges or whether an update was downloaded or applied.
The evidence does not independently establish the authenticity or integrity of the medledgerupd.exe binary.
The reason for the Chrome user-agent string on the updater-attributed proxy requests is not established.
unrelated_findings: Separate review may be warranted for tom.weber launching sqlcmd.exe with a query against dbo.Users on DB-SRV-01; the records show the command and a connection attempt to the server, but do not establish that the query succeeded or returned data (T086-00121, T086-00122, T086-00123, T086-00124).

Separate review may be warranted for a network logon to WS-TWEBER-01 from 10.51.10.24 as tom.weber; the records show a Kerberos ticket request from that address and a type 3 logon on the workstation, but do not establish who initiated it or whether it was authorized (T086-00062, T086-00063, T086-00064).

Other observed activity outside the alerted updater connections includes Chrome access to facebook.com and a Zoom background process; these records do not establish that either activity is malicious (T086-00054, T086-00098, T086-00094, T086-00095).
